authority.reference_observations: September 2025 Street View views from the WSW forecourt, northwest and southwest, plus an 18 July 2023 rear photograph from the east; private originals, not shipped
authority.detail_pass_observations: Exterior detail pass, 2026-11-20: dated 5 October 2008 public photographs (crescent frontal, three crescent window bays close, both canopy ends with the wings, south pavilion) and the National Register nomination's October 2003 photographs and text (Photographs 7-11; 'a full cantilevered stucco canopy decorated with scallop and beaded details', 'horizontal ribbing near the roof', 'corner pilasters'); private originals, not shipped
supported_public_family_cues: eleven two-story eighteen-light crescent windows between broad fluted piers with reeded heads
a deep cantilevered stucco canopy whose notched and reeded fascia meets the window sills, its ends sweeping back to the wall
rusticated projecting first floor with three glazed-bronze triple-door groups
eight upper and seven lower window bays per wing
projecting west-end pavilions with paired two-story twenty-light windows, flanks, flat-topped crowns over plain corner fins and aeronautical reliefs
crescent piers stopping under a plain frieze with incised lines and a thin coping
stepped multi-line cornices at the public roof edges
narrow upper windows over a continuous lower ribbon on the SE face, the ribbon wrapping the visible podium below a blank drum whose SE end bay holds one small and one tall opening

canopy.aerial_2025_note: The owner's 2025 aerial photos (daylight and dusk) show the canopy as a shallow slab of constant depth whose ends are cut square back to the wall with a small rounded outer corner, its fascia returning to the wall, stopping within about half a metre of the hall's corners; its top dark and weathered, with a raised lip along the edge and low ribs on the pier lines [seen]. Its depth, 4.4 m, is the map's canopy member's (front edge 4.4 m out from the hall wall line) [footprint]; the lip and rib sizes and the corner's radius are inference. In this model the hall's front wall stands on the map's canopy front edge (the generated footprint merges the canopy member into the building), so the slab is laid 4.4 m out from that wall.

read_from_photos: the canopy is deep enough to roof a walkway with seated sculptures under it, its soffit reading as an edge band, three panel rows and a wall band (2008 canopy ends)

its ends sweep round in a quarter turn back to the wall (2008 canopy ends; the owner's 2026-11-20 photos, south end) [replaced by the 2025 aerial photos: square-cut ends with a small rounded corner, see aerial_2025_note]

its soffit meets the wall 3.6 m over the door sills; its fascia, a stack of thin rolls about 0.55 m deep, stops about 0.9 m under the window frames, and black floodlight pucks stand on it at the piers (the owner's 2026-11-20 photos: the frontal and south-end views, scaled by the footprint's bay pitch)
a smooth pale soffit (the owner's 2026-11-20 frontal view)
production_inference: depth 5.0 m from the soffit's rows against the sculptures and walkway under it [replaced: 4.4 m, the map's canopy member, see aerial_2025_note]
the end turns' radius [replaced: end_corner_radius_m]
no rib within ribs.end_clearance_m of a square end, where it would run beside the end's lip (round 2: the owner saw a double line at the north end)
the fascia's five rolls as a mipmapped pattern
the floodlights' size

a group of three incised lines about 3.1-3.8 m over the frames and a thin flat coping about 5.6 m over them with one line in it (the owner's 2026-11-20 photos: the south-end and north-end views; 2008 frontal)

geometry_production_inference_m.pane_kinds_note: The glass's pane data (the material study, 2026-11-21): a pane's kind is the first rule for its part of the building (and its bottom's height) that takes it, by the rule's share of panes; else 1, a dark room. 2: a blind drawn down from the top; 3: sheers gathered to both sides.

read_from_photos: a white flagpole with a ball finial fixed to the crescent's attic face over the middle bay, in front of the coping band (its lower end shows below the coping's top edge in both of the owner's 2026-11-20 cupola photos, at the attic's top incised line), with a clamp on the coping band; about 6.7 m from its foot to the finial (both photos, from the camera poses solved on the crescent's windows)

The strip had run to the end face, leaving a free-standing wall there. The block's length follows the map's runs (production inference).

geometry_production_inference_m.se_shoulder_drum_join_note: The shoulder's south end met the taller crescent block behind it only across a slot about 0.7 m wide in plan, through which the sky showed along one line of sight (the 2026-11-21 visual check): drum_join fills it from the shoulder's inner face at that end, length_m along the face and depth_m inward, under the same coping, reaching into the taller block (production inference: the photos show the shoulder built against the drum). depth_m must reach into the taller block, about 0.75 m or more: the filler's coping has no inward overhang there, so its inner face, flush with the filler's, stays hidden only inside that block.

osm_exception.reason: The map's plan steps the north end of the hall front back to the wing in two radial steps with a 1.3 m jog (runs 17 to 20: the canopy member's notched end merged into the outline). The owner's 2025 aerial photos and 2026-11-20 photos show no such steps [seen]: the hall front, its attic lines and coping run on past the last pier as a blank panel about a bay wide to a plain square corner, and the hall's end wall runs straight back from that corner over the wing's roofs, one flat wall with its parapet and coping straight along it (the 2025 aerial photos, daylight and dusk [seen]). The plan here: the hall front's line carried on 3.93 m to the corner square across from the wing's start, then the end wall 10.45 m straight back from the corner, past the wing's start at 4.22 m (the departure from the map: about 15 m2 of plan outside its outline), to the line of the wing's set-back upper storey inside the mapped plan, and the back along that line to the hall block's end. The wing's set-down band's roof and riser run on to the end wall (5.0 m2 of roof, 1.68 m of riser), where the wing's strip gives up that plan. Shape and extent only: the building is not moved, rotated, merged, split or removed, and nothing outside the mapped outline reaches a neighbour, a road or placed street detail. The corner and the end wall's line follow from the wing's start [footprint]; where the end wall meets the set-back storey's line, and the back along that line, are production inference (the junction tower behind the end, in the photos, is not modelled).
osm_exception.approved: Owner, 2026-11-22: "The footprint should not be fixed if it is demonstrably wrong." (AGENTS: When dated photos contradict a footprint.) Round 3 on these corners: "The corner blocks still look odd. I think they should not be there at all, no?" Round 5, shown the end wall's bend where it followed the end of the wing's band: "Yes, straighten".
osm_exception.photo: The owner's 2026-11-20 photo of the hall's south end (its canopy's end, a door under it, the corner and the wing beyond), the owner's 2026-11-20 oblique view of the north end, and the owner's 2025 aerial photos, daylight and dusk, of both ends (all kept outside Git).

osm_exception.reason: The map's plan steps the south end of the hall front back to the wing in two radial steps with a 1.1 m jog (runs 39 to 43: the canopy member's notched end merged into the outline). The owner's 2026-11-20 photo of the south end and the 2025 aerial photos show no such steps [seen]: the hall front, its attic lines and coping run on past the last pier as a blank panel about a bay wide to a plain square corner, with a glazed door at its foot under the canopy's end and pavement in front, and the hall's end wall runs straight back from that corner over the wing's roofs, one flat wall with its parapet and coping straight along it (the 2025 aerial photos, daylight and dusk [seen]). The plan here: the hall front's line carried on 3.60 m to the corner square across from the wing's start, then the end wall 9.77 m straight back from the corner, past the wing's start at 3.61 m (the departure from the map: about 12 m2 of plan outside its outline, over the street ground's raised walk and planting strip mapped in the notch, which the street generator still draws under it), to the line of the wing's set-back upper storey inside the mapped plan, and the back along that line to the hall block's end. The wing's set-down band's roof and riser run on to the end wall (4.2 m2 of roof, 1.39 m of riser), where the junction's strip gives up that plan. Shape and extent only: the building is not moved, rotated, merged, split or removed, and nothing outside the mapped outline reaches a neighbour, a road or placed street detail (the nearest, a lot lamp, stands 0.6 m from the end wall). The corner and the end wall's line follow from the wing's start [footprint]; where the end wall meets the set-back storey's line, and the back along that line, are production inference (the junction tower behind the end, in the photos, is not modelled).
osm_exception.approved: Owner, 2026-11-22: "The footprint should not be fixed if it is demonstrably wrong." (AGENTS: When dated photos contradict a footprint.) Round 3 on these corners: "The corner blocks still look odd. I think they should not be there at all, no?" Round 5, shown the end wall's bend where it followed the end of the wing's band: "Yes, straighten".
osm_exception.photo: The owner's 2026-11-20 photo of the hall's south end (its canopy's end, a door under it, the corner and the wing beyond), the owner's 2026-11-20 oblique view of the north end, and the owner's 2025 aerial photos, daylight and dusk, of both ends (all kept outside Git).

hall_ends.corner_note: Round 4 (the owner: "The corner is still slightly curved as far as I can tell, and it should just be straight"): each end panel was already one straight run from the last pier to the corner, but the attic skin, its lines and the coping were shaded smoothly round the corner, so its top read as rounded; they now turn it square (HALL_END_CREASE_DEG in building_1_hero_model.gd), as the owner's 2026-11-20 photo of the south end shows the lines and coping turning a sharp corner. Round 5 (the owner, shown the bend where each end wall followed the end of the wing's band, 16 degrees north and 13 south: "Yes, straighten"): each end wall now runs straight back from its corner to the line of the wing's set-back upper storey, so the attic turns only at the corners.

south_tier_fill.note: The owner, round 2: the two wings should look alike on top. The south wing's third storey was two 11 m strips (front and rear) with a gap about 3.5 m wide between them open down to the two-storey roof, read from the air as a second step; the 2025 aerial photos show one unbroken upper roof [seen]. The gap is roofed at the third storey's height, its end at the wing's start cap walled.

geometry_production_inference_m.south_junction_wedge_note: The south junction tower's strip and the south wing's strip end on two caps from one corner whose runs' normals differ by about 4 degrees, so they part into a wedge 0.71 m wide at its mouth, open to the sky. Over the wing's set-down front the wing's cap stood alone with open air behind it, and along one grazing line of sight its culled back showed the wedge and the sky past it (the interior shell check, 2026-11-22). A solid box along the wing's cap fills the wedge: its face proud_m proud of the cap, its far side overlap_m into the tower's strip, its back end rear_inset_m inside the mouth; its top lies flush with the roofs either side and is drawn with them in the roof's material (round 2: a pale top read as a wedge on the roof). Round 3: in front of the wing's riser (wing_setback.setback along the cap) the south hall end (hall_ends) stands over the wedge, so the box starts there. Round 5: the south hall end's wall runs straight back from its corner, so before the riser the wedge lies under the band's roof carried on to that wall, the tower's and the wing's caps cut there; the box starts HALL_END_WEDGE_BEHIND_RISER_M (0.02 m) behind the riser's line, out of the plane of the riser carried on before it. Production inference: the 2025 aerial photos show the wing built against the junction block with no gap.
